# Tab siblings keep reordering while the drag is far outside their strip

## Context

Operator, 2026-10-23 ~17:05Z, his manual test of the v13.3.1 head (an 11 s screen recording), filed as minor by him: he drags the Metrics tab, whose strip has one sibling (Audit), out of the header and across the window; while the pointer is far outside the strip, the Audit header keeps sliding left and right *"as if it was an in-header drag"*.

**Design constraint (operator, 17:1xZ):** this is a dock-layout defect, not a toolbar one. In a default tab container with sortable headers and no other drop zones (`examples/tab/container`), the reorder continuing after the pointer leaves the boundary container is wanted behaviour and stays. Only a strip that takes part in dock drag parks its reorder.

The live app (his Chrome window, Neural Link session `6cc72d13…`, dev c393d9f544) shows the mechanism in the sort zone's own trace (`get_drag_trace`, zone `neo-dock-tab-sortzone-4`, owner `neo-tab-header-toolbar-5`, items `neo-tab-header-button-16` / `-17`, strip at y ≈ 150):

| ts | pointer | `over` | event |
|---|---|---|---|
| …142685 | (920, 224) | false | `switch` 0 → 1 |
| …144116 | (894, 447) | false | `switch` 1 → 0 |
| …145468 | (918, 499) | false | `switch` 0 → 1 |
| …146537 | (899, 470) | false | `switch` 1 → 0 |

Four sibling swaps, every one with the pointer 75–350 px below the strip, each when the pointer's **x** crossed the sibling's midline; the gesture then landed as a dock drop (Metrics split beside Priority Alert Observatory in the left pane; frames 17–23), and the sort zone's terminal was `end from 0 to 0, noop`. The first recording of the day carries the same class in the heavy-tabs strip: `switch` 5 → 4 at y 294 and 4 → 3 at y 573 while `over: false` (the #20070 trace, gesture 3).

Frames 5–9 of the recording: the Audit header sits at the strip's right end, then at its left, then right again, while the ghost and the "Moving pane to another window…" vessel travel the window.

Sweeps: the newest 20 open issues at 16:52Z and the claims of the last hour, no equivalent (#20070 is the other finding of this test; Ada's #19986 / #19987 / #19988 from 10-22 are the adjacent strip-drag defects: the maximized-pane edge preview, the overflow recapture paint, the flying header); Memory Core (`query_raw_memories` on the symptom): those three, none is this.

## The Problem

The within-toolbar reorder is a one-axis machine. `Neo.draggable.container.SortZone#onDragMove` (`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:723-845`) reads `isOverDraggingStart` / `isOverDraggingEnd` only along the sort axis (`:755-761`: `clientX` beyond the boundary's left or right for a horizontal strip) and otherwise swaps siblings whenever the pointer's delta along that axis exceeds `moveFactor` of the neighbour's width (`:812-823` → `switchItems`, `:1074`). Nothing in that path asks whether the pointer is still anywhere near the strip on the cross axis. For a plain sortable toolbar that is the right contract: the user keeps control of the order with a loose hand, and there is nothing else the gesture could mean.

A dock strip is different. The dock's `TabSortZone` enables overdrag and the drag proxy may leave the container (tear-out), so a dock drag spends most of its life far from the strip where it means a dock operation, and every horizontal crossing of a sibling's midline down there animates the strip as if the drag were in-header.

The release already knows the difference: `TabSortZone#releaseVoidsReorder` (`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs:523-532`) declares a release farther than `dockReleaseTolerance` (32 px, `:108-114`) beyond the toolbar's real bounds *"dock-gesture territory"* and voids the tracked reorder there, so the drop lands right. Only the hover contradicts it: the siblings move for a reorder the release will void. The tear-out path even has the parking mechanism: `startWindowDrag` parks the base reorder and `endWindowDrag` *"un-parks"* it (`:256-263`); the in-window, out-of-strip phase of a dock drag never parks.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs`: `onDragMove` `:723-845` (axis-only over-drag at `:755-765`, the swap branches `:782-823`, the trace emitter `:826-838`), `switchItems` `:1065+`, `sortBoundaryRect` `:134-137`, `boundaryContainerRect` and the tear-out hysteresis `:376-482`. **Its over-boundary reorder is a contract, not a defect:** `src/draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` (the default tab-header zone) and `examples/tab/container/MainContainer.mjs` rely on it, as do the grid header's sortable buttons (`test/playwright/unit/grid/HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs`).
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs` (the dock strip, a different class): `dockReleaseTolerance` `:108-114`, `enableCrossZoneDrag` `:125-127` (the dock-participation flag the release path already gates on, `:682`, `:688`, `:703`), `sortGroup` `:120-122`, `releaseVoidsReorder` `:510-532` (pure over instance state, built to be driven per event), `startWindowDrag` / `endWindowDrag` `:237-263` (the existing park / un-park of the base reorder), `onDragMove` `:729-763` (feeds the coordinator and the dock hover, then `super.onDragMove`), `processDragEnd` `:594-700` (consumes `releaseVoidsReorder`).
- The dock host paints its own hover (`DragAffordances`), so parking the dock strip's reorder loses no affordance: the user sees the dock preview, not a reorder. A plain toolbar has no such host, and its reorder is the only affordance; that is the operator's distinction in code.

Design authority: `releaseVoidsReorder`'s contract (beyond the tolerance band is dock territory) and the tear-out's park / un-park, both already gated on `enableCrossZoneDrag`. The hover should show what the release will do, in the one zone whose release has two meanings.

## The Fix

In `TabSortZone` only, gated like the release (`enableCrossZoneDrag !== false`): park the base reorder while the pointer is outside the strip's tolerance band, un-park it when the pointer returns, so the hover matches the release.

1. `TabSortZone#onDragMove`: evaluate `releaseVoidsReorder({clientX, clientY})` per move. Entering dock territory parks the within-toolbar reorder the way `startWindowDrag` does (siblings return to their resting order, `currentIndex` back to `startIndex`, no further `switchItems`) while the proxy keeps moving and the coordinator / dock hover keep receiving the frame; re-entering the band un-parks it (`endWindowDrag`'s half), and the reorder resumes from the live pointer. If the base needs a seam for "move the proxy but do not reorder", add it to `SortZone` as the single opt-in flag the tear-out park already implies, default off, so no base consumer changes behaviour.
2. The release path is unchanged: `releaseVoidsReorder` still decides, and a release inside the band still commits the reorder the un-parked hover tracked.
3. `draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone`, `examples/tab/container` and the grid header keep today's over-boundary reorder untouched.

Red-first: a unit arm over the dock strip with a two-item strip, a pointer that leaves the band and crosses the sibling's midline (today: a `switch` in the trace; after: none, and the sibling's rect is its resting rect), then re-enters and crosses it (a `switch` again); the same sweep over the default tab-header zone keeps its `switch` (the control that pins the operator's distinction); a throttled e2e arm in `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/` performing the operator's gesture (Metrics out of a two-tab strip, a horizontal sweep 300 px below it, a dock drop elsewhere) asserting the Audit header's rect never changes while the pointer is below the band and the dock drop still lands.

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 **Unit, red-first (dock strip):** a two-item horizontal dock strip, a drag of item 0 that moves 300 px below the strip and sweeps across item 1's midline: the trace carries no `switch`, item 1's rect is its resting rect; on dev today the same sweep emits `switch 0 → 1`.
- [ ] AC-2 **Re-entry:** the same drag brought back into the band (within `dockReleaseTolerance`) and swept across the midline reorders (`switch`), and a release there commits the reorder; a release outside the band after a sweep commits nothing (the void, unchanged).
- [ ] AC-3 **Default toolbars unchanged (the operator's distinction):** the same sweep over `draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone` (the `examples/tab/container` zone) and over the grid header's sortable buttons still emits `switch` and commits the reorder on release outside the boundary container; the existing within-toolbar reorder arms stay green; a dock drag that never leaves the band behaves exactly as on dev.
- [ ] AC-4 **E2E, the operator's gesture, red-first under throttle:** Metrics out of a two-tab strip, a sweep 300 px below it across Audit's midline, a dock drop into another pane: Audit's header rect is constant for every frame below the band on the head (on dev it changes), and the dock drop lands as before.
- [ ] AC-5 **Live (PMV):** the operator repeats his gesture on the merged head and the Audit header does not move until the pointer is back at the strip; the `examples/tab/container` headers still follow a loose hand.

## Out of Scope

- The base `SortZone`'s over-boundary reorder for plain toolbars: wanted, kept.
- The tear-out vessel's own choreography (`startWindowDrag` / `endWindowDrag`), beyond reusing its park.
- Ada's adjacent strip defects (#19986, #19987, #19988).
- Vertical strips: the fix is axis-agnostic by construction (`releaseVoidsReorder` pads the real rect on all sides), but no vertical consumer is on the tester's path.

## Avoided Traps

- **Fixing it in the base `SortZone`:** would take the loose-hand reorder away from every plain toolbar and tab container; the operator named that behaviour as wanted.
- **Clamping the proxy to the strip:** the dock drag must leave the strip; the proxy is right, the sibling animation is wrong.
- **Voiding at release only (today):** the drop is already right; the hover lies for the whole gesture.
- **A new distance threshold:** `dockReleaseTolerance` is the band the release uses; the hover must use the same number or the two disagree again at the edge.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-23T17:24:29Z

Intake: **valid-as-written**, accepted, building now. Two facts the build settles, for the reviewer:

1. **The base needs the seam Fix step 1 left conditional.** The tear-out park is `isWindowDragging` short-circuiting `SortZone#onDragMove` through `checkWindowBoundary` (`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:400-485`). That call only runs with `enableProxyToPopup`, which the adapter sets for tear-out compositions alone (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1422`, `context.enableDockTearOut === true`). An in-window dock strip has no such path, so the base gets one class field, `isReorderParked` (default `false`), read in `onDragMove` right after the window-boundary check. Only the dock strip arms it, so every base consumer keeps today's behaviour.
2. **The resting-order restore is new.** `startWindowDrag` (`TabSortZone.mjs:360-373`) never returns the siblings or `currentIndex`; it only stops further switches and the commit. The park walks the tracked switches back with `switchItems`, which undoes itself for a neighbour pair (`test/playwright/unit/draggable/container/SortZone.spec.mjs:773`, "repeated switches in both directions do not drift the geometry").

Line drift on dev `c29f694f9e`: `endWindowDrag` is `:263-270`, `startWindowDrag` `:360-373`.
